title: quest agents --check reports state: current while the opum-quest plugin is disabled and no skill file exists, so --require-installed cannot distinguish a plugin-shipped skill from no skill at all (DEC-238 a3)
description:
Filed from DEC-238 (a3), opum-doc ruling 2026-10-25T06:54:02Z (record: opum-doc PR chore/dec-238-a2), which says verbatim: "quest-cli files the parallel bug: `quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude` reports current while the plugin is off."

MEASURED in this checkout on 2026-10-25, before filing:
$ quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude
plugin:
  id: opum-quest@opum
  remedy: claude plugin enable opum-quest@opum --scope user
  runtime: claude
  scope: user
  state: disabled
  version: 0.13.0
skill:
  state: current
state: current
exit=0

Corroborating state: `claude plugin list --json` reports opum-quest@opum enabled=false scope=user; `.claude/skills/` does not exist at all; `.lore/config.toml` sets skill_source = "plugin". So no quest skill file exists in this checkout, while the check concludes `current` and exits 0.

WHY THIS IS THE LORE DEFECT PARALLEL: for lore, a disabled plugin means the skill is absent, and `lore agents --check` exits 0 anyway — which DEC-238 (a2) (1) corrected by making the diagnostic lines the criterion rather than the exit code. Here the same exit code carries the same non-signal: `state: current` is reported while the plugin is disabled and no skill file exists.

WHAT IS DOCUMENTED, so the plan does not misread this as a regression: `quest help agents` (QCLI-371) says `data.plugin` reports installed/disabled/not-installed/not-detectable and that plugin state only reports and prints a remedy; it also says plainly that neither changes the exit code. `skill: state: current` under skill_source = "plugin" plausibly means "declared plugin-sourced, nothing to generate", which is consistent — but the top-level `state: current` is then read as "the workspace is current" in a checkout where there is no skill at all.

DECISION NEEDED AT PLAN TIME, and it is opum-doc call, not this repository own: whether `--require-installed` should account for a disabled plugin, or whether the output and help must state that `state: current` describes the managed CLAUDE.md block only. DEC-238 (a3) fixes the surrounding fact that quest guidance reaches workers through each CLAUDE.md managed quest block, and that no repo-local quest skill is restored (ODOC-142 retired it); re-enabling opum-quest is the operator call under DEC-172 (4bf), not part of this fix.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The `quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude` output states that `state: current` covers the managed CLAUDE.md block only, not plugin enablement, in both the human and the --json forms
The exit code is unchanged by a disabled plugin: QCLI-371 semantics are preserved and no carve-out is introduced for DEC-172 (4bf)
A test pins the disabled-plugin case and its exit code, so the output shape and the wording cannot change silently
`quest help agents` and the manifest text for --require-installed and data.plugin match the output wording
The change neither enables opum-quest nor restores a repo-local quest skill: DEC-172 (4bf) keeps the plugin off at user scope, and DEC-238 (a3) leaves quest guidance on the managed block

definitionOfDone.text: The fix lives in the check or its documentation, not in this repository CLAUDE.md
QCLI-371 exit-code semantics are either preserved deliberately or changed with the help text updated in the same change
The measured before-state from this record is re-run after the change and cited both ways

implementationNotes:
DEC-238 (a4) Point 3, opum-doc ruling 2026-10-25T07:18:35Z (record: opum-ai/opum-doc#1355, lands on dev when green), RULED A, verbatim: "the exit code is unchanged, and the output states that `state: current` covers the managed block only, not plugin enablement. B is not adopted: it would fail every fleet checkout while opum-quest is off by the operator DEC-172 (4bf), forcing a carve-out or a reversal."

So the arm this task implements is the reporting arm, not a semantic change: the check keeps exiting 0 with a disabled plugin and says what `state: current` is a statement about. Criteria 1-4 encode exactly that; criterion 5 records the boundary B would have crossed.

Measured before-state, 2026-10-25T07:01Z (to be re-run after the change, both ways):
  $ quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude
  plugin: id: opum-quest@opum, remedy: claude plugin enable opum-quest@opum --scope user,
          runtime: claude, scope: user, state: disabled, version: 0.13.0
  skill: state: current
  state: current
  exit=0
  $ claude plugin list --json  ->  opum-quest@opum enabled=false scope=user
  $ ls .claude/skills/         ->  No such file or directory
  $ quest help agents          ->  data.plugin reports installed/disabled/not-installed/not-detectable
                                   and "neither changes the exit code" (QCLI-371)
